stem:
In the past, one quarter of job applicants at a certain firm had first-class degrees. A change is made in the job description and a director of the firm believes that, on average, the proportion of job applicants with first class degrees has decreased.

In the month following the change, there were 35 job applicants, and $r$ of these had first-class degrees. The firm carried out a hypothesis test at the 4% significance level to test the director’s belief.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Use a binomial distribution to find the largest value of $r$ that would provide sufficient evidence that the director’s belief is correct.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: In another month, the director carries out a similar test at the 4% significance level using the 35 job applicants from that month.
parts.text: Explain the meaning of a Type I error in this context, and state the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Given that the proportion of job applicants with first class degrees this year is actually 0.05, find the probability of a Type II error.
